lines: Clock-synced LFO: one cycle is the clock period multiplied and divided by whole numbers, with a sine, a triangle, a sawtooth and a square running from it.
Sets how many times faster than the clock the cycle runs, a whole number from 1 to 128.

Sets how many clock periods one cycle lasts, a whole number from 1 to 128.
Sets how much of the voltage at the DIVISION input is added to the division number, from full inverted to full; 10V at full adds 128.

Rounds the phase setting to the nearest quarter cycle, so 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees; the light is lit while that rounding is on.
Chooses the range of every output: -5V to 5V, or 0-10V.
Chooses what the cycle does while the outputs are frozen: keep advancing underneath, so the wave jumps on release, or pause and carry on from where it stopped.
Chooses how the HOLD input is read: each trigger turns the freeze on and off, or the freeze lasts only while that input is at 1V or more.
Chooses how the CLOCK input is read: as pulses whose spacing sets the period, or as a BPM voltage where 0V is 120 BPM and each volt doubles the tempo.
Sets the tempo everything else is multiplied and divided against; with nothing patched here the outputs do not move.
Voltage added to the multiply number through its attenuverter.
Voltage added to the division number through its attenuverter.
Voltage shifting the start of the cycle through its attenuverter.
A trigger here restarts the cycle at the phase setting.
Freezes the outputs at their last value, either toggled by each trigger or held while this is at 1V or more, as the GATE and MOM. switch is set.
The sine wave at the clocked rate.
The triangle wave at the clocked rate.
The sawtooth wave at the clocked rate.
The square wave at the clocked rate, half of every cycle high and half low.

lines: Megalomanic Compression: five band compressor, each band with its own detector, threshold and gain, mixed back to stereo.
Switches that band in and out of the mix.
Sets the corner frequency of that band, marked in Hz, from about 8Hz to 16700Hz; the default is 261.63Hz.
Adds to that band's corner frequency, 10V covering the full sweep before the attenuverter.
Widens that band around its corner frequency, 0 to 100%; band one is a low pass and band five a high pass, so neither has one.
Adds to that band's width, 10V covering the full range before the attenuverter.
Sets the level that band's detector acts on, -50dB to 0dB; the default is -30dB.
Sets how hard that band's gain is pulled back past the threshold, 1:1 to 20:1.
Sets how fast that band's gain reacts to a signal crossing the threshold, 0.02ms to 100ms.
Sets how fast that band's gain recovers once the signal falls back, 40ms to 5 seconds.
Bends that band's attack from exponential through linear to logarithmic, -1 to +1.
Bends that band's release from exponential through linear to logarithmic, -1 to +1.
Softens the corner at that band's threshold, 0dB to 10dB wide.
Switches that band's detector between instantaneous peak reading and an averaged RMS reading.
Sets the length of the averaging window that band uses in RMS detection, 0.02ms to 50ms.
Switches that band between pulling back signals above its threshold and lifting signals below it.
Lifts the level going into that band's detector, 0dB to 30dB, without changing the signal that passes through.
Lifts that band's compressed signal back up, 0dB to 30dB; in upward mode the same amount is taken off instead.
Adds CV to one compressor setting in one band, summed with the knob and scaled by that setting's attenuverter.
Scales the CV for the control it serves, -100% to 100%; negative settings invert the CV.
A trigger here flips the switch it serves; a menu option turns these into gate inputs instead.
Feeds that band's detector from this signal instead of the band's own audio.
That band's filtered signal, source or sidechain, for driving the detector of another band or anything else.
Drives that band's gain from another detector's envelope in place of its own.
That band's gain reduction as a voltage, rising as more reduction is applied.
That channel of a signal fed straight into that band's compressor, skipping the filter stage.
That channel of that band's compressed signal on its own, before the bands are summed.
Encodes the two inputs as mid and side, compresses there, and decodes back to left and right.
Compresses the mid part while mid-side mode is on; with this off the mid passes at its own level.
Compresses the side part while mid-side mode is on; with this off the side passes at its own level.
Passes the inputs straight to the outputs with no compression and no makeup gain.
Blends the dry input with the summed compressed bands, 0 to 100% compressed; the default is 100%.
Adds to the wet/dry blend, 10V covering the full range before the attenuverter.
The left signal to be compressed; with nothing patched to the right input, this one feeds both channels.
The right signal to be compressed; leaving this unpatched sends the left input to both channels.
Feeds every band's detector from this signal instead of the inputs, filtered by each band before it is read.
That channel of the summed bands, blended with the dry input by MIX.
Menu — Envelope Mode — how the envelope output is scaled, one of Linear - Gain Reduced, Linear or Exponential; the last two put out very high voltages at large gain reductions.
Menu — Gate Mode — reads the CV inputs of the switches as gates rather than as triggers.

lines: Splits a polyphonic pitch CV into whole semitones and the leftover fraction, so a plug-in in Host can play microtonal scales.
The polyphonic pitch to be split; every channel patched in is carried through to both outputs.

The part of the pitch above that whole semitone, as 0-5V per channel; set the plug-in's pitch bend range to one half step.
Note — it sends no MIDI of its own: patch its two outputs into a Host module's CV and pitch bend inputs, then set the hosted plug-in's pitch bend range to one half step either way.

lines: Records incoming gates as MIDI note events and saves them to a MIDI file; each of the sixteen columns sets the note one gate channel plays.
Sets the MIDI note number that column records, 0 to 127.
Sets the velocity that column records, 0 to 127; the default is 64.
Spreads the recorded velocity randomly, by half this many steps either side of the velocity setting.
Sets the MIDI note number that column records while its accent channel is above 0V, 0 to 127.
Sets the velocity recorded for an accented gate on that column, 0 to 127; the default is 110.
Spreads the accented velocity randomly, by half this many steps either side of the accent velocity setting.
Adds to the note number, 127 steps over 10V; the module reads only the first column's jack and applies it to every column.
Adds to the velocity, 127 steps over 10V; the module reads only the first column's jack and applies it to every column.
Adds to the velocity spread, 127 steps over 10V; the module reads only the first column's jack and applies it to every column.

Adds to the accent velocity, 127 steps over 10V; the module reads only the first column's jack and applies it to every column.
Adds to the accent velocity spread, 127 steps over 10V; the module reads only the first column's jack and applies it to every column.
Starts recording, and stops it on the next press; starting clears everything already recorded.
A trigger here starts recording, and the next trigger stops it.
Sets the tempo the events are timed against, 0V giving 120BPM and every volt doubling it.
The gates to be recorded; each channel of a polyphonic cable is recorded on the column of the same number.
Marks a gate as accented while this is above 0V; each channel matches the gate channel of the same number.
Note — the BEATS display counts quarter notes since the first recorded event, and the NOTES display counts the events recorded so far.
Menu — Save MIDI File — writes what has been recorded to a .mid file at a place you choose.
Menu — Ticks per Quarter Note — the timing resolution written into the file, one of 96, 240, 441, 480, 882, 960, 15360 (Cubase) or 16384 (Bitwig).
Menu — Load Drum Map — reads a file of names for the note numbers; the names appear in the columns only while Use Note Names is ticked.
Menu — Clear Drum Map — drops the loaded drum map, so the columns go back to note names or numbers.
Menu — Use Note Names — prints the note columns as note names rather than as MIDI note numbers.

Sets how far the input signal pulls down the level of the delayed taps, 0 to 100%. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.

Audio into the delay for that channel; with only the left jack patched, it feeds both channels.
Carries the dry input and the delayed taps for that channel, blended by MIX.
Inverts the phase of the delayed signal in that channel, leaving the dry signal alone.
Sets how much of the feedback signal is added back into the delay input, 0 to 100%. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Sets how far the input signal pulls down the level of the feedback, 0 to 100%. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Tones the feedback: below halfway a lowpass closes from 100kHz down to 10kHz, above halfway a highpass rises from 10Hz to 100Hz. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Reverses the direction the buffer is read, over a window as long as the feedback time. The button toggles it; a patched signal toggles or gates it, set by the mode switch.
Feeds the left feedback into the right channel and the right into the left. The button toggles it; a patched signal toggles or gates it, set by the mode switch.
Chooses how a patched voltage is read for that function: as a trigger, flipping the setting on each rising edge, or as a gate, holding it on while the voltage is above 0V.
Chooses which of the 16 taps feeds the feedback in that channel; one step past the last tap takes the sum of every tap, and the step after that, EXT, takes its time from the FB TIME input.
Moves the feedback read point in that channel ahead of or behind its tap time by up to half a tap. A patched voltage adds 10% per volt.
Shifts the pitch of the feedback in that channel by up to 24 semitones either way, in whole semitones. A patched voltage adds 2.4 semitones per volt.
Detunes the feedback in that channel by up to 99 cents either way. A patched voltage adds 10 cents per volt.
Sets the feedback delay time from a voltage, 1ms to 10 seconds, and is read only while the feedback tap control is set to EXT.
Carries the feedback signal for that channel after its tone shaping, before it is returned to the delay input.
A signal patched here replaces the feedback in that channel, which is how an effect is placed in the feedback path.
Steps through four ways of limiting the feedback: unlit is off, red clips at 6V, yellow compresses at 20 to 1, green compresses adaptively.
Gives that tap the delay time of the next tap along, so the two sound together, which is how chords are built; a run of stacked taps all take the time of the last one.
Silences that tap, fading it out over 100 samples rather than cutting it.
Sets the level of that tap, 0 to 100%.
Places that tap between left and right, full left to full right. A voltage patched to that tap's pan input moves its pan by 20% per volt and its level by 10% per volt.
Chooses the filter on that tap: off, lowpass, highpass, bandpass or notch.
Sets the cutoff of that tap's filter, 15Hz to 8400Hz; it does nothing while that tap's filter is off. A patched voltage adds a tenth of the range per volt.
Sets the resonance of that tap's filter, 0.5 to 50; it does nothing while that tap's filter is off. A patched voltage adds 5 per volt.
Shifts the pitch of that tap by up to 24 semitones either way, in whole semitones. A patched voltage adds 2.4 semitones per volt.
Detunes that tap by up to 99 cents either way. A patched voltage adds 10 cents per volt.

PortlandWeather.notes: Nothing in the module reads the grid input, the sixteen tap level inputs, or the two phase reverse inputs; all nineteen are configured and drawn, and no line of process() touches them. The mute, stack, ping pong and reverse inputs have no fixed threshold: with the matching trigger mode switch on gate they are read above 0V, and on trigger they go through a Schmitt trigger at 1V.

lines: Probably Not(e) is a probabilistic quantiser: the incoming pitch goes to the nearest of twelve notes, then a note near that one is chosen at random, weighted by the note weights of the key and scale.
Sets how many notes either side of the quantised note can be chosen, 0 to 6; at 0 the quantised note is the only candidate.
Sets the direction of the choice: fully left only notes below the quantised note, centre both directions, fully right only notes above.
Sets the starting probability across the candidates: at 100% every candidate is equally likely, at 0% the furthest candidate falls to a tenth of the chance, rising linearly towards the centre.
Rotates the scale's note weights up or down by as many as eleven steps, which moves the weighting between modes of a scale, C major to A minor for instance.
Chooses one of 42 scales, from Chromatic and Whole Tone through the seven modes to Blues, Hirajoshi, Persian and Ukrainian Dorian.
Sets the root the scale is built on, C through B.
Shifts the quantised note by whole octaves, -4 to +4.
An attenuverter, -100% to +100%, scaling the voltage at the input it belongs with before that voltage is added to the control's own setting.
Puts the note weights and the on or off state of the current scale back to the values that scale ships with.
Holds every chosen note inside the octave of the pitch at NOTE IN when lit, so a B below a C comes out eleven semitones above it; unlit, chosen notes land near the incoming pitch.
Steps the tuning of the output through equal temperament, pure whole-number ratios and Pythagorean tuning.
Steps through how WEIGHT SHIFT reads its input: unlit is one step of shift per volt, and the two lit states read a volt per octave, one relative to the key and one absolute so that 0V shifts to C.
Makes the KEY input read a volt per octave when lit, so the key can follow a keyboard or another quantiser; unlit, 0-10V spans the twelve keys.
Bends the note weights from linear at 0% to logarithmic at 100%, which widens the gap between likely and unlikely notes.
Detunes the chosen note by a random amount of as much as 10 cents.
Draws the pitch randomisation from a Gaussian distribution when lit, from an even one when unlit.
Gives each polyphonic voice its own channel of the TRIGGER input when lit; unlit, every voice is clocked from the first channel.
Takes that note out of the scale or puts it back; a note that is off is never chosen.
Sets the probability weight of that note within the current scale, 0 to 100%; in most of the scales the root and the fifth start highest.
Sets the chance that the note last played is barred from being chosen again; at 100% a note never repeats.
Takes each chosen note out of the pool until every available note has been used, then refills the pool.
The pitch to be quantised, a volt per octave; its polyphony sets how many voices the module runs.
Voltage here is added to the setting of the control it belongs with, scaled by that control's attenuverter.
Voltage here moves through the list of 42 scales, 0-10V spanning the whole list at a full attenuverter.
Voltage here moves the key, 0-10V spanning the twelve keys, or a volt per octave when v/O is lit.
A trigger here switches between equal temperament and whichever other tuning is selected.
A trigger here chooses a new note; with nothing patched here no new note is chosen.
Takes the random number behind the note choice from this voltage, 0-10V, instead of the module's own; each polyphonic channel feeds the matching voice.
A trigger here turns octave wrapping on or off.

lines: PW - ALGORITHMIC EXPANDER — generates the tap times for a Portland Weather placed immediately to its left, replacing its groove patterns with a rhythm built from an algorithm.
Steps through three ways of placing beats: yellow is Euclidean, blue is a Golomb ruler, green is a well formed rhythm of long and short steps.
A rising edge here steps through the three ways of placing beats.
Sets how many steps the pattern is divided into, 1 to 16. Taps beyond that count, and taps on steps with no beat, are muted.
Adds to the number of steps in the pattern, 1.6 steps per volt.
Sets how many beats are placed across the steps, 0 to 16; in Golomb ruler mode it chooses which ruler is used.
Adds to the number of beats placed across the steps, 1.5 beats per volt.
Rotates the whole pattern round by up to 15 steps, moving every beat along together.
Rotates the pattern round, 1.5 steps per volt.
Holds up to 15 steps at the start of the pattern empty, and packs the beats into the steps that are left.
Adds to the number of empty steps at the start of the pattern, 1.5 steps per volt.
Sets the ratio between the long and short steps of a well formed rhythm, and does nothing in the other two modes.
Adds to the ratio between long and short steps, 10% per volt.
Note — the pattern is timed from the clock and division of the Portland Weather it is attached to, so a clock has to be patched there for the taps to move.
Note — it can be chained after a PW Tap Breakout expander, but not before one.

Sends the drawn values to the pitch shift of the 16 taps, up to 24 semitones either way, replacing their pitch knobs.
Sends the drawn values to the detune of the 16 taps, up to 99 cents either way, replacing their detune knobs.
Note — drag in the grid to set one value per tap. Several of these expanders can be chained, one per destination.

lines: Four tracks of algorithmic rhythm, up to 73 steps each, with beat, accent and end of cycle triggers; under the manual algorithm you click a track's step display to place its beats.
Sets the number of steps in that track's pattern, 1 to 73.
Voltage adds to the number of steps in that track, 7.3 steps per volt on top of the knob setting.
Sets how many beats are spread through that track's steps, none to one per step. Under the Boolean algorithm the number picks the operator: 1 AND, 2 OR, 3 XOR, 4 NAND, 5 NOR, 6 NXOR.
Voltage adds to the number of beats in that track, 7.3 beats per volt on top of the knob setting.
Rotates that track's beat pattern forward by a number of steps, 0 to 72, so it starts somewhere other than step 1.
Voltage adds to the rotation of that track's beat pattern, 7.2 steps per volt on top of the knob setting.
Holds that many steps at the start of the track empty, 0 to one less than the step count; the algorithm spreads the beats over the steps left.
Voltage adds to the number of empty steps held at the start of that track, 7.2 steps per volt on top of the knob setting.
Sets how many of that track's beats are accented; the accent algorithm chooses which ones, and they fire from that track's accent jack.
Voltage adds to the number of accented beats in that track, 7.3 accents per volt on top of the knob setting.
Rotates that track's accent pattern along its beats, so the accents land on different beats of the same rhythm.
Voltage adds to the rotation of that track's accent pattern, 7.3 beats per volt on top of the knob setting.
Steps through the algorithm that places that track's beats: Euclidean, Golomb ruler, well formed, perfect balance, manual, Fibonacci, and on tracks 3 and 4 Boolean logic on the two tracks above.
A trigger steps that track on to the next beat algorithm.
Steps through the algorithm that places the accents among that track's beats: Euclidean, Golomb ruler, perfect balance, manual, Fibonacci, and on tracks 3 and 4 Boolean logic.
A trigger steps that track on to the next accent algorithm.
Frees that track from the master chosen with track sync, so it keeps its own step rate and plays a polymetre against the other tracks.
A trigger starts that track when chain mode is Boss or Employee. Left unpatched with QARs side by side, the end of cycle of the one to the left arrives here.
A 1ms 10V trigger on each beat of that track.
A 1ms 10V trigger on each beat of that track that carries an accent.
A 1ms 10V trigger when that track reaches the end of its pattern.
A 1ms 10V trigger at the end of each pass through the groove pattern, when a QAR Groove expander is applied to that track.
The clock the tracks run on, one step per pulse; the gap between the last two pulses sets how long a step lasts.
Sets the tempo of the module's own clock, doubling per volt from 120 BPM at 0V; the menu's BPM x4 multiplies that by four.
Starts and stops the module's own clock, which runs only while something is patched into the BPM jack.
A trigger starts or stops the module's own clock, which runs only while something is patched into the BPM jack.
Sends every track back to the start of its pattern, firing the next beat at once. Held with the shift key it clears the timing, swing, warp and conditional counts as well.
A trigger sends every track back to the start of its pattern; with Reset to Step 0 ticked in the menu it clears the timing and expander state as well.
Stops every trigger output while the tracks keep running; pressing it again lets the triggers through.
A trigger stops every trigger output while the tracks keep running; another trigger lets them through again.
Steps through what the tracks fit their timing to: nothing, track 1, 2, 3 or 4, or the X steps count, which is how one track of 15 can run against another of 11.
Sets the number of steps, 1 to 360, that the tracks fit their patterns into when track sync is set to X steps.
Voltage adds to the step count the tracks fit into under X steps sync, 36 steps per volt.
Runs the tracks from the clock without waiting for a start trigger.
Runs the tracks at startup, then holds any track whose start input is patched until a start trigger arrives; this is the setting for the first QAR in a chain.
Holds every track idle until a trigger arrives at its start input.
Recalls the settings stored in that scene for this module and for every QAR expander attached to it. With saving armed it stores them there instead.
Arms saving, so the next scene button pressed stores the settings of this module and its expanders into that scene rather than recalling them.
Selects a scene from voltage, one scene per 1.25V starting at 0V, and recalls what is stored there.
Note — no track steps until a clock is patched into the clock input, or a voltage is patched into the BPM input and the run button is switched on.
Note — with a track's algorithm set to Manual, click that track's ring in the display to turn a beat on or off, and hold shift while clicking to turn an accent on or off.
Menu — Reset to Step 0 — ticked, a trigger at the reset input clears all the timing as well as the beat; unticked, it moves the beat to step 0 and leaves the timing alone.
Menu — BPM x4 — reads the BPM input as four times the tempo it otherwise gives.

Voltage raises or lowers every value in the grid at once, 5V for the full range.
Voltage rolls the drawn shape along the 18 steps and wraps it around, 5V for the whole way.
Multiplies every grid value by the cosine of the setting, so the shape flattens to nothing halfway round and comes back inverted at the ends.
Voltage adds to the grid rotation, 10V for its full travel.
Cycles five pinning modes: off; values at or below the pin held at it; those values left where they are while the rest move; values at or above the pin held at it; those left where they are.
Sets the value the pinning modes measure against, 0% to 100% of the grid's range.
Voltage adds to the pin position, 10V for the full range.
Note — drag across the grid to draw one value per step, 18 in all, which the expander it is attached to uses in place of its own per-step settings.
Menu — All Maximum, All Minimum, All Half, Triangle, Sine, Ramp and Random — shapes drawn into the grid; these are on the grid display's own right-click menu, not the panel's.
Menu — Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical, Reduce By Half, Shift Left and Shift Right — changes to the shape already drawn; these are on the grid display's own right-click menu, not the panel's.

Makes the groove pattern run the same length as the track it is applied to, in place of the length setting.
Switches the pattern from following steps to following beats, so its entries land on the 1st beat, 2nd beat and so on whichever steps those fall on.
